name: PsExec.exe
description: PsExec is a free Microsoft tool that can be used to execute a program on another computer. It is used by IT administrators and attackers.
summary: Remotely create accounts on target systems
Leverage Windows services to escalate privileges from administrator to SYSTEM
Download or upload a file over a network share
Writes programs to the ADMIN$ network share to execute commands on remote systems
Execute binaries on remote systems using a temporary Windows service

associated_apts.name: Indrik Spider
associated_apts.description: Indrik Spider used PsExec to leverage Windows Defender to disable scanning of all downloaded files and to restrict real-time monitoring. Indrik Spider has used `MpCmdRun` to revert the definitions in Microsoft Defender. Additionally, Indrik Spider has used WMI to stop or uninstall and reset anti-virus products and other defensive services. Indrik Spider has used PsExec to stop services prior to the execution of ransomware. Indrik Spider has encrypted domain-controlled systems using BitPaymer. Additionally, Indrik Spider used PsExec to execute a ransomware script.

associated_apts.name: Medusa Group
associated_apts.description: Medusa Group has utilized PsExec to facilitate execution, lateral movement, defense evasion, and exfiltration. Medusa Group has terminated antivirus services utilizing the gaze.exe executable and utilizing `psexec.exe`. Medusa Group has also leveraged I/O control codes (IOCTLs) for terminating and deleting processes of identified security tools. Medusa Group has utilized PsExec to execute scripts and commands within victim environments. Medusa Group has also used the Windows service RoboCopy to search and copy data for exfiltration. Medusa Group has utilized compromised legitimate local and domain accounts within the victim environment to facilitate remote access and lateral movement sometimes in combination with PsExec. Medusa Group has utilized PsExec to execute batch scripts that modify firewall settings. Medusa Group has also enabled and modified firewall rules to allow for RDP connections for lateral movement and device interactions. Medusa Group has utilized PsExec to execute `quser` to discover the user session information.
